JUDGMENT

This is petition filed under Section 164 of Motor Vehicles Act, 1988, seeking compensation of Rs.10,00,000/- from the respondents, on account of death of Aslam Basha S., who is husband of petitioner No.1 and father of petitioner No.2, in a road traffic accident.
2. The brief facts of the case are as follows :
On 29-12-2022 at about 00.45 a.m., the deceased Aslam Basha was riding a NTORQ scooter bearing Reg. No.KA-03-KL- 4840 from Madanapalli to Bengaluru.

When he reached near Chikkahulluru, Chintamani, he drove the same with high speed, in rash and negligent manner and lost control over his vehicle and fell down along with his scooter infront of Taj Hotel.
Due to the said impact, he has sustained fatal injuries.

Immediately after the accident, he was shifted to Silicon City Hospital, Bengaluru,
wherein he took first aid treatment and then he was shifted to Sifaa Hospital.
He succumbed to said injuries on 31-12-2022 at about 11.00 a.m., while he was undergoing treatment in the said hospital.
Earlier to the accident, the deceased was working as auto driver and earning a sum of Rs.30,000/- per annum.
He was contributing his entire earnings to his family.
Due to untimely death of a sole bread earner, the petitioners are struggling for their livelihood.
The Hoskote Police have registered the case for the offences punishable under Section 279, 337 and 304(A) of I.P.C.
The respondent No.1 is the owner and respondent No.2 is the insurer of the offending vehicle.
Hence, they are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the petitioners.
Therefore, it is prayed to allow the petition and award compensation of Rs.10,00,000/- with interest at the rate of 12% per annum.

2 3.
On service of notice to the respondents, the respondents No.1 and 2 have appeared through their counsel.
The respondent No.2 has filed its written statement.
Whereas, the respondent No.1 did not choose to file his written statement.
4. The respondent No.2 in its written statement has denied all the allegations made in the petition.
It has admitted the issuance of insurance policy in respect of motorcycle bearing No.KA-03-KL-4840 and its validity as on the date of accident.
It seeks protection under Sections 147, 149(2) and 150(2) of Motor Vehicles Act.
It has contended that, the petition is bad for non compliance of provision under Sections 134(c) and 158(6) of Motor Vehicles Act.
Further, it has sought for permission to contest even on behalf of respondent No.1 under Section 170 of the Motor Vehicles Act.
Further it is contended that, in the said accident only one vehicle was involved and the deceased himself was riding the bike, skidded and fell down and he himself is the tortfeasor to the accident.
The complaint was filed against the deceased and after conducting investigation, the police have filed the charge-sheet against Syed Aslam Pasha for his rash and negligent driving.

The legal representatives of the accused/tortfeasor have filed the present petition under Section 164 of the Motor Vehicles Act, for the wrongful act of the accused/tortfeasor, which is not maintainable.
Further it is contended that, as per Section 164 of the Motor Vehicles Act, the claim petition is not maintainable if only one vehicle is involved in the accident.
There must be 2 or more vehicles involved and the claim of tortfeasor must be against another vehicle which was involved in the said accident.
But, in the present case there is no other vehicle involved in the accident.
The tortfeasor cannot file a claim petition against the insured and insurer in which he was driving the vehicle, as he is not a 3rd party.
The tortfeasor cannot claim for his own negligence under Section 164 of Motor Vehicles Act.

Further it is contended that, the accused/tortfeasor rode the two-wheeler bearing No.KA-03-KL-4840, without holding valid and effective driving licence to ride said vehicle, as on the date of the accident.

The accused was holding driving licence with respect to only 3 wheeler-cab,
which was valid from 12- 11-2019 to 11-11-2024.
The insured has violated the terms and conditions of the insurance policy as well as Motor Vehicles Act provisions and hence, he is not liable to pay any compensation to the petitioners.
For the above denials and contentions, it prayed for dismissal of the petition.

5. On the basis of rival pleadings of both the sides, the following issues are framed:
ISSUES 1.

Whether the petitioners prove that, the deceased Aslam Basha S. S/o Late S.
Abdulla Basha has succumbed to the injuries sustained in a road traffic accident,
arose out of the usage of NTORQ Scooter bearing registration No.KA-03-KL-4840,
alleged to have occurred on 29-12-2022 at about 00:45 A.M., near Chikkahulluru,
Hosakote Taluk, Bengaluru Rural District ?
2. Whether the petitioners are entitled to compensation?

If so, what is the quantum and from whom ?
3. What order or Award ?

In order to prove their case, the petitioner No.1 has got examined herself as P.W.1 and got marked total 16 documents as Ex.P.1 to Ex.P.16.

They have also examined one more witness by name K.S.
Shivaprasad as P.W.2.

On the other hand, the respondent No.2 has examined its representative/Associate Legal Claims as R.W.1 and Superintendent of R.T.O., Bengaluru East as R.W.2 and got marked total 5 documents as Ex.R.1 to 5.
The respondent No.1 has not adduced any evidence on her behalf.
7. I have heard the arguments of both the sides and perused the entire material placed on record.

8. My findings on the above issues are as under:
Issue No.1: Negative Issue No.2: Negative Issue No.3: As per the final order, for the following:
REASONS 9. Issue No.1: It is the specific case of the petitioners that, on 29-12-2022 at about 00.45 a.m., the deceased Aslam Basha was riding a NTORQ scooter bearing Reg. No.KA-03- KL-4840 from Madanapalli to Bengaluru.

When he reached near Chikkahulluru, Chintamani, he drove the same with high speed, in rash and negligent manner and lost control over his vehicle and fell down along with his scooter, infront of Taj Hotel and sustained fatal injuries.
Later he succumbed to said injuries, on 31-12-2022 at about 11.00 a.m., while he was undergoing treatment at Sifaa Hospital.
Further it is contended that, earlier to the accident, the deceased was working as auto driver and earning a sum of Rs.30,000/- per annum.
He was contributing his entire earnings to his family.
Due to untimely death of a sole bread earner, the petitioners are struggling for their livelihood.
10. In order to prove their case, the petitioner No.1 has got examined herself as P.W.1 by filing examination-in-chief affidavit, wherein she has reiterated the entire averments made in the petition.
Further, in support of their oral evidence, the petitioners have got marked total 16 documents as Ex.P.1 to 16.

Out of the said documents, Ex.P.1 is certified copy of F.I.R., Ex.P.2 is certified copy of spot mahazar, Ex.P.3 is certified copy of sketch, Ex.P.4 is certified copy of Motor Vehicles Accident report, Ex.P.5 is certified copy of inquest, Ex.P.6 is certified copy of post- mortem report, Ex.P.7 is certified copy of charge-sheet, Ex.P.8 to 10 are notarized copies of Aadhar cards of petitioners No.1 and 2 and deceased, Ex.P.11 is notarized copy of ration card, Ex.P.12 are medical bills (total 8),

Ex.P.13 is authorization letter, Ex.P.14 is true copy of medical certificate, Ex.P.15 is true copy of death report and Ex.P.16 is case-sheet.
11. On meticulously going through the above police documents marked as Ex.P.1 to 7, prima-facie it reveals that, the alleged accident has taken place due to rash and negligent riding of the deceased/rider of offending scooter bearing Reg. No.KA-03-KL-4840.

Due to rash and negligent riding, the deceased has lost control over his vehicle and fell down on the road, sustained fatal injuries on his head and succumbed to said injuries on 31-12-2022 at about 11:00 a.m., while undergoing treatment at Shifaa Hospital, Bengaluru.

The investigation officer in his final report/charge-sheet, marked as Ex.P.7, has clearly stated that, the said accident is taken place due to Rehana Begum vs Tasleem.M on 3 October, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/61956931/

12. At the outset it is pertinent to note that, in the present case, the date, time and place of accident,
involvement of NTORQ scooter bearing Reg. No.KA-03-KL-4840 in the said accident, issuance of insurance policy by the respondent No.2 in respect of said scooter and its validity as on the date of accident, are not in dispute.

Further it is pertinent to note that, the petitioners themselves have unequivocally admitted in their petition itself that, at the time of accident the deceased Aslam Basha was riding his scooter with high speed, in rash and negligent manner and due to which he has lost control over his vehicle and fell down along with his scooter and sustained fatal injuries.

This clearly goes to show that, admittedly there was no other vehicle involved in the said accident and the said accident has taken place due to rash and negligent riding of the deceased himself and it is a self-fall accident.
As such, the deceased himself was the tort-feasor.

13. Further, the Ex.P.2 spot mahazar and Ex.P.3 sketch also clearly speaks that, the said accident has taken place in the middle of 20 feet wide Chintamani-Hosakote road, infront of Taj Hotel, near Chikkahulluru village, Hosakote taluka, Bengaluru District, due to skid and fall of the scooter bearing Reg. No.KA-03-KL-4840 of the deceased.
Further, as per the Motor Vehicle Accident Report, which is marked as Ex.P.4, the accident has not taken place due to any mechanical defects in the vehicle involved in the accident.

When the accident was not caused due to the any mechanical defects in the vehicle involved in the accident, then in the present facts and circumstances of the case, it clearly establishes that, the said accident had occurred due to rash and negligent riding of the deceased.
The Ex.P.6 post-mortem report, clearly speaks that, the deceased Muthuraju has died due to hemorrhage and head injury sustained in the road traffic accident.
Further, the investigation officer in his final Ex.P.7 final report/charge- sheet has clearly stated that, the said accident is taken place due to rash and negligent riding of the deceased himself.
Admittedly, the said charge-sheet has not been challenged either by the petitioners or by the owner of said vehicle.

In such circumstances,
there is no impediment to believe the final report of the investigation officer and other police records, regarding the date, time and place of accident, involvement of the offending vehicle, rash and negligent riding of the scooter bearing Reg. No.KA-03-KL-4840 by the deceased, injuries caused to the deceased in the said accident and cause of his death.

14. Therefore, for the above stated reasons, this Court is of the opinion that, the petitioners have successfully proved that, deceased Aslam Basha S. S/o Late S. Abdulla Basha has succumbed to the injuries sustained in a road traffic accident, occurred on 29-12-2022 at about 00:45 A.M., near Chikkahulluru, Hosakote Taluk, Bengaluru Rural District, arose out of the usage of scooter bearing registration No.KA-03-KL-4840.
Hence, I answer Issue No.1 in Affirmative.
15. Issue No.2:
The petitioners are claiming compensation under Sec.164 of Motor Vehicles Act.
The liability under Sec.164 of Motor Vehicles, 1988, is on the principle of no fault.

The petitioner need not require to establish that, the death is caused due to any wrongful act or negligence or default on the part of the driver of the vehicle involved in the accident or of the concerned or of any other person.
The Sec.164 of Motor Vehicles (Amendment) Act, 2019, reads as follows:
Rehana

5 164. Payment of compensation in case of death or grievous hurt, etc. - (1)
Notwithstanding anything contained in this Act or in any other law for the time being in force or instrument having the force of law, the owner of the motor vehicle or the authorised insurer shall be liable to pay in the case of death or grievous hurt due to any accident arising out of the use of motor vehicle, a compensation, of a sum of five lakh rupees in case of death or of two and a half lakh rupees in case of grievous hurt to the legal heirs or the victim, as the case may be.

( 2 ) In any claim for compensation under sub-section (1), the claimant shall not be required to plead or establish that the death or grievous hurt in respect of which the claim has been made was due to any wrongful act or neglect or default of the owner of the vehicle or of the vehicle concerned or of any other person.

(3) Where, in respect of death or grievous hurt due to an accident arising out of the use of motor vehicle, compensation has been paid under any other law for the time being in force, such amount of compensation shall be reduced from the amount of compensation payable under this section.
16. No doubt, the liability under Sec.164 of Motor Vehicles, 1988, is on the principle of no fault liability.
But, the said provision is applicable only to the third party, as the said provision fall under Chapter XI of Motor Vehicles Act, 1988.
The very heading of/title of Chapter XI (covering section 145 to 164-D) is Insurance of Motor Vehicles Against Third Party Risks.
Therefore, the provision under Sec.164 of Motor Vehicles Act, 1988, is applicable only to a person/victim other than the insurer and the insured and his driver/agent.

In the present case, since the deceased himself was riding the motorcycle is not a third party under the Motor Vehicles act and/or under the requirement of insurance policy, the respondent No.2 insurance company is not liable to pay compensation to the petitioners under the provision of Sec.164 of Motor Vehicles Act, 1988.

Further,
it is held that, when there was no relationship of employer and employee between the owner of scooter bearing No.KA-03-KL-4840 and the deceased, the respondent No.2 insurance company cannot be fastened with any liability, as the owner of said vehicle is not vicariously liable.
The deceased cannot be a third party in relation to a vehicle which he himself was using/riding.

17. Further it is pertinent to note that, the petitioners have unequivocally admitted in their petition itself that, at the time of accident the deceased Aslam Basha was riding his scooter with high speed,
in rash and negligent manner and due to which he has lost control over his vehicle and fell down along with his scooter and sustained fatal injuries.

This clearly goes to show that, admittedly there was no other vehicle involved in the said accident and the said accident has taken place due to rash and negligent riding of the deceased himself and it is a self-fall accident.
Further, the Ex.R.5 Driving Licence Extract clearly speaks that, the deceased was not holding driving licence to ride two wheeler vehicle, as on the date of accident.
As such, the deceased himself was the tort-feasor.

It is settled principle of law that, a tortfeasor cannot claim compensation under Sec.164 of Motor Vehicles Act,
as the said provision provides a fixed compensation amount for victims or their legal heirs for death or grievous injury caused in the road traffic accident.
But, it does not apply to those who have caused the accident through their owner wrongful act or negligence.
The core principle is that, a person cannot be both the wrongdoer and the entitled recipient of compensation for the same incident.

Therefore, in such circumstances and for the above stated reasons, this Court is of the opinion that,
the petitioners are not entitled for any compensation from the respondents, in respect of death of Aslam Basha S., in a road traffic accident, took place on 29- 12-2022 at about 00:45 A.M., near Chikkahulluru village, Hosakote Taluk, Bengaluru Rural District, arose out of the usage of scooter bearing registration No.KA-03-KL-4840.

Hence, I answer Issue No.2 in Negative.
18.
Issue No.3

: In view of the above findings, I proceed to pass the following order:
ORDER

The petition filed by the petitioners under Sec.164 of Motor Vehicles Act,
1988, is dismissed.
No order as to costs.
Draw award accordingly.
